similarly to a stream cipher, with the added
benefit of self-synchronization.

question: Of the following, which is NOT a logical error?

options.A: Using the '=', instead of '===' to determine if two values are equal
options.C: Failing to initialize counter and total variables before the body of loop
options.D: Using commas instead of two required semicolons in a for loop header

solution:
The correct answer is option D.
A logical error is a bug in a program that causes it
to produce incorrect or unexpected results.
"Using commas instead of two required
semicolons in a for loop header" is not a logical
error as it is a syntax error and the rest of the
three are logical errors.

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : A load-and-go assembler avoids the overhead of writing the object program out and reading it back in.
Reason ( R ) : This can be done with either one-pass or two pass assembler.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.A: Both ( A ) and ( R ) are true and ( R ) is the correct explanation of ( A )
options.B: Both ( A ) and ( R ) are true but ( R ) is NOT the correct explanation of ( A )
options.D: (A) is false but ( R ) is true

solution:
The correct answer is option A.
Load-and-go assemblers generate their object
code in memory for intermediate execution. No
object program is written out, no loader is
needed.
Assertion (A): A load-and-go assembler avoids
the overhead of writing the object program out
and reading it back in.
This statement is true. A load-and-go assembler
directly loads the program into memory and
executes it without creating an intermediate
object file, thus eliminating the overhead
associated with writing to and reading from
storage.
Reason (R): This can be done with either a one-
pass or two-pass assembler.
